_comment: Corpus index coverage ratchet (DATA, not code). ADR-0541 Corpus Liveness Graph. A buck2 package that OWNS at least one YAML file is INDEXED iff it declares a corpus-yaml-facts extraction target, which makes that YAML a build-graph input whose facts are a build output. Two ceilings, both shrink-only: baseline_uncovered_packages is the in-graph debt (packages that could be indexed today and are not), and baseline_unpackaged_yaml_files is the NORTHSTAR debt (YAML files belonging to no buck2 package, which cannot be indexed at all until they are pulled INTO the build graph). The second ceiling is deliberately the larger number: indexing an artifact through a side channel would improve a coverage score while leaving it outside the graph, so the gate counts unpackaged files in the DENOMINATOR and never lets a side channel look like progress. The two min_expected_* floors are the anti-vacuity backstop: a walk that silently sees nothing reports zero uncovered files, which reads as PERFECT coverage, so a collapsed census fails the gate closed. baseline_unpackaged_yaml_files is EQUALITY-pinned rather than one-sided — above it is a regression, below it is an unattributed drop — because a fall in the northstar term is either real progress or a mis-attributing walk and the counts cannot tell those apart. ALL repo-specifics are DATA — another repo adopts this gate by repointing these four numbers.

product_contract.born_advisory: Born ADVISORY over today's debt and BLOCKING on regression. 18 YAML-owning packages declare no extraction target and 83 YAML files sit outside every buck2 package; both are reported as advisory findings and frozen as ceilings. A NEW uncovered package, or NEW YAML outside the build graph, exceeds its ceiling and fails closed.
product_contract.shrink_only: Both ceilings are lowered as extraction targets and service-root packages land. The gate emits a corpus_index_stale_ceiling advisory whenever a ceiling sits above the measured number, so slack cannot silently accumulate and absorb the next regression.
product_contract.pack_shaped: The Rust kernel hardcodes no oyatie path. Package census, file census, and both ceilings are DATA.
product_contract.anti_vacuity: min_expected_yaml_packages and min_expected_yaml_files fail the gate closed when the walk collapses. Without them a broken walk reports zero uncovered packages, which is indistinguishable from full coverage. Both guard the CENSUS. Neither guards the ATTRIBUTION, because both are invariant under mis-attribution: if every file were wrongly assigned to some package, packaged rises by exactly what unpackaged loses, the package count is unchanged, and the total floor still holds while the unpackaged term — the one the northstar ratchet rides on — reads zero and looks like the debt being paid off. That gap used to be covered by a THIRD floor, min_expected_unpackaged_yaml_files, and bead oyatie-ln1 established that the floor was structurally defective rather than mis-set: it asserted a minimum on a term whose northstar is ZERO, so honest progress tripped it, six consecutive waves had to lower it, and the final wave could not have satisfied it at all. The floor is DELETED. The attribution guard is now two-sided equality on baseline_unpackaged_yaml_files: a drop below the ceiling is blocking until the ceiling is re-frozen in the same change, which forces a human to state whether artifacts really entered the graph. It fails closed on the same collapsed walk the floor caught, it is monotone in the same direction as the programme's own goal, and zero is a stable fixed point of it.
product_contract.known_limitations: Source-derived extraction faces use the canonical BUCK AST parser but are not a Starlark evaluator, so configured Buck2 targets/uquery parity remains mandatory. Only the YAML artifact class is measured; markdown, JSON, TOML, and Cedar each need their own extractor and their own ceiling.

purpose: Make 'everything in the code graph and the build graph' a measured, shrink-only invariant instead of a slogan, by counting indexed vs total artifacts and letting the number move in only one direction.
